chunks: You've definitely heard of this cafe.
Britannia and Company, Ballard Estate.
Serving lunch since nineteen twenty three.
An Iranian immigrant, Rashid Kohinoor, opened it.
His son Boman took over at twenty,
and kept it going until he died at ninety seven.
And there's one reason people still make the trip.
The berry pulao.
Saffron rice, chicken or mutton,
and tart barberries, still brought in from Iran.
So, worth the trip? Yes. Definitely.
Order the berry pulao, take your time,
and sit inside a hundred years of old Bombay.
Public rating, four point two.
Lunch only, closed by four on weekdays,
shut on Sundays. Bring cash, and go hungry.
Then it's a short walk to Bombay Coffee House,
for your next stop.
